title: Burnham Starts Transforming Britain
text:
Burnham Starts Transforming Britain

Anatole Kaletsky

Gavekal Research | 30 Sep 2026

Andy Burnham, the new British prime minister, on Tuesday confirmed the transformation of British politics which was made possible by his replacement of the inept Keir Starmer and which is an indispensable condition for Britain’s economic revival (see Britain’s New Leader Could Bring New Hope). Burnham’s speech to the Labour Party conference, which the Financial Times aptly described as “breathtaking in scale and determination,” announced a cutback in pension spending that was unthinkable under Starmer. More importantly, it showed an openness to possible U-turns in fiscal policy, EU relations and electoral reform, along the lines suggested on the day of the 2024 election landslide as necessary conditions for a Labour government to have any chance of success (see ‘Change Election’ Changes Nothing).Since I have been anticipating for the past 12 months that a U-turn on some or all of these issues would act as a catalyst for a turnaround in Britain’s dismal economic and financial performance (see Turning Bullish On Britain (But Not On The Labour Party)), my bias is to view this speech as a pivotal moment for the UK economy and a bullish inflection point for sterling assets. While the initial market reaction to Burnham’s speech was indifference or skepticism, there are three reasons why the skeptics are likely to be proved wrong, and why this really could be a turning point in Britain’s financial fortunes:
